entries.name: Cable Crunch
techniqueCitations: Contreras, B. (2014). Bodyweight Strength Training Anatomy. Human Kinetics, pp. 110-115.
Coburn, J. W., & Malek, M. H. (2012). NSCA's Essentials of Personal Training (2nd ed.). Human Kinetics, pp. 370-371.
entries.reason: Redrawn on 8 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing contradicted this text: it showed a stiff trunk hinging forward at the hips. Source-bound side-view draft with a spine that curls: kneeling facing a high pulley with the rope at the collarbones; the hips and the lower back do not move while the upper spine rounds and the elbows travel toward the thighs, then it unrolls more slowly. The figure kneels leaning toward the pulley, which is high and a short way in front, so the cable only lengthens on the way down.
entries.summary: Kneeling with the rope at your collarbones, round the upper spine to drive the elbows toward the thighs with the hips frozen, then unroll slowly.

frames.caption: Kneel far enough from the stack that the cable stays loaded at the top, rope held to your collarbones.
Crunch by rounding your upper spine, driving your elbows towards your thighs while your hips stay frozen.
Round the upper spine, elbows to the thighs.
Unroll slowly until the abs are on stretch.
Hips locked in place. Abs pull, arms just hold the rope.

entries.name: Crunch - Hands Overhead
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing was against this text: the trunk lifted as one stiff piece. Source-bound side-view draft with a spine that curls: lying with the knees bent and the feet flat, arms long beside the head; the hips and the lower back stay on the floor while the upper spine curls until the shoulder blades are just off it, the arms staying in line with the head, a pause, and a slower lowering. Not drawn: the hands together, which a side view cannot show.
entries.summary: Lying with the knees bent and the arms stretched overhead, curl the upper body up until the shoulder blades are just off the floor with the arms in line with the head, pause, then lower slowly.

frames.caption: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat, arms stretched overhead with the hands together.
Keeping the arms in line with the head, curl the upper body up until the shoulder blades are just off the floor.
Pause. Curl the ribs toward the hips.
Lower slowly to the start.
Arms stay in line with the head.

entries.name: Crunches
entries.reason: Own drawn frames on the same supine crunch chain with the hands at the temples and the torso riding a drawn bench pad (the template names a bench; a floor crunch would not answer how the equipment is used - recorded at the checkpoint). Full notes and open questions in the daily review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a bench crunch with the hands at the

frames.caption: Lie back on the bench with the hands lightly at the temples.
Brace before moving, then curl the shoulders up.
Complete the trunk action through a range you can own.
Pause with the pelvis set and the trunk braced.
Own the return without momentum.
Lower the shoulders back to the bench slowly.

entries.name: Rope Crunch
entries.reason: Own drawn frames on the same supine crunch chain with the hands holding a rope at the chest on a cable to a drawn low pulley at the feet side. Full notes and open questions in the daily review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a supine rope crunch with the cable l

frames.caption: Lie back holding the rope at the chest with the cable live.
Curl the ribs toward the pelvis with the rope steady.
Pause with the abdominals shortened.
Hold the curl without letting the rope pull the arms.
Lower on a slow count against the cable.
Return the shoulders to the floor with control.

entries.name: Sit-Up
entries.reason: Source-bound side-view draft with a spine that curls. Knees bent, feet flat, hands crossed on the chest; the trunk peels off the floor from the head end while the lower back is still down, then the whole curled trunk comes up until the chest meets the thighs, and it rolls back down the same way in the same time. The trunk is drawn along the curled spine, not as one stiff piece pivoting at the hips, which the source calls a different movement.
entries.summary: Knees bent and feet flat, curl the torso up one segment at a time until the chest meets the thighs, then roll back down the same way.

frames.caption: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, hands crossed on your chest.
Curl your torso up one segment at a time until your chest meets your thighs.
Exhale on the way up.
Roll back down the same way, as slowly as you rose.
Peel up one vertebra at a time.

entries.name: Tuck Crunch
entries.reason: Source-bound side-view draft with a spine that curls. Hips and knees bent with the shins level, arms reaching toward the feet; the upper spine curls so the shoulders come up while the knees travel a little toward the chest, a pause, then both ends lower slowly together. Not drawn: the pelvis tilting toward the ribs. The lower back stays on the floor in this drawing and the knees carry that half of the movement.
entries.summary: Hips and knees bent, arms reaching toward the feet: curl the shoulders up as the knees travel slightly toward the chest, pause, then lower both ends slowly.

frames.caption: Lie on your back with the hips and knees bent and the arms reaching toward the feet.
Bring the ribs and pelvis toward one another, curling the shoulders up as the knees travel slightly toward the chest.
Pause with the abdominals shortened. Reach past the hips.
Lower both ends slowly.
Lower both ends on the same slow count.

entries.name: Reverse Crunch
entries.reason: Source-bound side-view draft with a spine that curls. Knees bent over the hips, hands flat beside the body, shoulders on the floor; the lower spine curls so the pelvis rolls up and the hips leave the floor, with the legs riding on the pelvis and keeping their shape, then the hips lower more slowly. The feet stay off the floor for the whole cycle.
entries.summary: Knees bent over the hips, roll the pelvis up so the hips leave the floor and the knees come towards the ribs, then lower the hips slowly without the feet touching down.

frames.caption: Lie on your back with knees bent over your hips, hands flat beside you.
Curl your hips off the floor, bringing the knees towards your ribs: the pelvis rolls up, the legs do not swing.
Roll the pelvis up towards the ribs.
Lower the hips back down slowly.
Keep the feet floating between reps.

entries.name: Cable Reverse Crunch
entries.reason: Source-bound side-view draft with a spine that curls. Lying with the head away from the stack and a low cable to the ankles, hips and knees at right angles, shoulders on the floor; the pelvis tucks first, then the lower spine curls so the tailbone lifts and the knees come toward the ribs, with the legs riding on the pelvis, and the hips set down more slowly. The cable stays taut and only lengthens as the knees come in. Not drawn: the ankle cuffs; the cable ends at the ankle.
entries.summary: Lying with a low cable on the ankles, tuck the pelvis, curl the knees toward the ribs until the tailbone lifts, then set the hips down slowly with the cable still tight.

frames.caption: Attach both ankles to a low cable, lie facing away from the stack, hips and knees near 90 degrees, shoulders heavy on the floor.
Tuck the pelvis first, then curl the knees toward the ribs until the tailbone lifts without throwing the legs.
Curl the knees toward the ribs.
Set the hips down slowly while keeping cable tension.
Start with the pelvis tucked.

entries.name: Bent-Knee Hip Raise
entries.reason: Source-bound side-view draft with a spine that curls. Lying flat with the arms beside the body, knees bent 75 degrees and the feet just clear of the floor; the knees are drawn toward the chest at that same knee angle, then the lower spine curls so the pelvis rolls back and the hips leave the floor, a one-second hold, and a slower return to the start.
entries.summary: Lying flat with the knees bent and the feet just off the floor, draw the knees toward the chest at the same knee angle until the hips leave the floor, squeeze for a second, then lower slowly.

frames.caption: Lie flat on the floor with the arms beside you, knees bent to about seventy-five degrees and the feet a couple of inches up.
Draw the knees toward the chest, holding that knee angle, until the pelvis rolls back and the hips leave the floor.
Squeeze at the top for a second.
Lower slowly to the start.
Hold the knee angle throughout.
